title: Project overview
transcript:
01 / PROJECT OVERVIEW
FIRST UNITY PROJECT.
BUILT TO MOVE FAST.
MY ROLE
PROGRAMMER +
IMPLEMENTATION
Dash Drive is a 3D endless runner where the 
player controls a sports car across three traffic 
lanes, dodging vehicles and obstacles while 
pushing for a higher score and distance. The 
route progresses from a suburban district into a 
dense city section, with a police pursuit acting as 
a boss encounter in each area.
Two-person team. My teammate 
created the visual artwork and models 
while I handled all programming, Unity 
implementation, gameplay systems, UI 
integration and technical assembly.
PROJECT OUTLINE
We were tasked to create a 3D 
endless runner with multiple 
obstacles, two distinct sections or 
“levels”, and a boss encounter for 
each section.
2 PERSON TEAM
Pierre Louw - Programmer
Nick Smart - Artist
ENGINE
UNITY
LANGUAGE
C#
TOOLS
UNITY + BLENDER

title: Core gameplay
transcript:
02 / CORE GAMEPLAY
THREE LANES.
The core loop is deliberately simple: read the road, switch 
lanes, avoid traffic and keep the run alive.
CORE LOOP  →  READ  /  SWERVE  /  AVOID  /  SCORE

title: Two environments
transcript:
03 / TWO ENVIRONMENTS
FROM SUBURBIA
TO THE CITY.
The run is split into two visually distinct environments that 
repeat after each other to break repetition.
SECTION 01 / SUBURBS
Open residential roads, houses, trees and wider 
sightlines introduce the player to the challenge.
SECTION 02 / CITY
Denser buildings and a tighter visual corridor 
create a faster, more intense second half of the 
run.

title: Boss encounters
transcript:
04 / BOSS ENCOUNTERS
AVOID
THE POLICE.
Each environment ends with a timed 
police pursuit. Instead of a traditional 
enemy fight, the boss encounter 
changes the pressure to make the 
player survive the chase, keep moving 
and avoid being caught.
BOSS OBJECTIVE
SURVIVE FOR
A SET TIME
Police pressure replaces the normal 
pacing and creates a clear climax for 
each section.

title: Player controls & world spawning
transcript:
05 / MY CONTRIBUTION
BUILDING THE GAME LOOP
AND PUTTING THE WORLD TOGETHER.
My focus was turning the artwork into a complete playable game: 
implementing movement, endless progression, obstacle logic, scoring, boss 
events, UI, settings and the overall gameplay loop in Unity using C#.
01
PLAYER CONTROLS
I implemented a dynamic-feeling 
steering control system where 
the player’s car stabilizes itself 
after a lane change. It does this 
by steering the front tyres to 
correct the oversteer.
02
ENVIRONMENT SPAWNING
Surrounding plots of land are 
spawned ahead of the player and 
subsequently despawned after 
the player has passed. 
Conversely, there are a set 
amount of road pieces that are 
rotated to the front of the list.

title: Traffic & boss systems
transcript:
05 / MY CONTRIBUTION
BUILDING THE GAME LOOP
AND PUTTING THE WORLD TOGETHER.
03
TRAFFIC + OBSTACLE SPAWNING
Traffic is spawned in a random 
lane ahead of the player. 
Construction zones can spawn 
on either of the side lanes and at 
different lengths as they are built 
with construction road pieces.
04
BOSS EVENTS
After the player has covered a 
certain distance in the current 
area, the boss section is 
spawned. In this section all traffic 
stops spawning and subsequent 
police obstacles are spawned in 
random lanes.

title: UI & settings
transcript:
05 / MY CONTRIBUTION
BUILDING THE GAME LOOP
AND PUTTING THE WORLD TOGETHER.
05
UI + SETTINGS
The HUD, menus, settings, and 
leaderboard screens use the 
Nova framework for design and 
logic.

title: Learning Unity
transcript:
06 / LEARNING
THE PROJECT THAT
TAUGHT ME UNITY.
Dash Drive was my first complete project in 
Unity. Building it required learning C# in the 
context of a real game, understanding Unity’s 
component workflow, integrating 3D assets, 
debugging gameplay systems and connecting 
multiple features into one coherent build.

title: The future
transcript:
07 / THE FUTURE
DASH DRIVE’S FUTURE.
We will continue to add more features and maps/areas into the game. The 
plan is to release the game on mobile devices sometime in 2027.
